findings.description: The PR rewrites decision 0183's landed sentence in place instead of appending an amendment.
findings.body:
**`docs/adr/README.md` §Reading and writing: landed-text-immutable**

Decision 0183 was already on `main` at the merge base (`ee7c5b3`). Its text there read: *"Turning a step on reaches the next launch, and the next respawn of a running task, never a window already running."* This PR replaces that sentence in place.

The ADR README, lines 19–21, says:

> Once a decision has landed, a later change appends an amendment section to it (dated, with the PR) or adds a new decision that links back through `Amends:`. It does not rewrite the landed text.

The README makes no exception for factual corrections. The same commit follows this rule for 0165, where it restores the landed `path:line` text and adds a dated amendment that supersedes it. 0183 should get the same treatment. Keep the landed sentence, then add a dated amendment (`2026-11-14, #334`) that says a rework step reaches the next launch or fix round, because a respawn resends the stored context and recompiles nothing. The correction itself is accurate: `src/core/session-handoff.service.ts` recompiles nothing on respawn, and `compileSessionProfile` in `src/core/session-lifecycle.service.ts` runs for both launches and fix rounds.

<https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/924d5ab00ab87ced233265fbad2c83a4520eac05/docs/adr/0183-a-rework-step-s-setting-is-a-store-file-read.md#L15-L18>
findings.suggestion:
*Read at compile time.* Turning a step on reaches the next launch, and the next respawn of a
    running task, never a window already running. The kickoff it changes is hashed, so turning it
    on or off marks the live sessions' profiles stale, as a brief edit does. It changes no gate.
    *The respawn (2026-11-14, #334).* This supersedes the respawn claim above: turning a step on
    reaches the next launch or fix round, never a window already running, because a respawn
    resends the stored context and recompiles nothing.
